close_reason: Not a bug: when policy_mapping==0, nodes with issuer_domain_policy are deleted, then prune_policy_tree() removes orphaned ancestors. stale expected_policy_set is cleaned up by pruning.
description:
When policy_mapping == 0 (mapping inhibited), nodes with issuerDomainPolicy as valid_policy are deleted at lib.rs:1863-1878. However, PARENT nodes at cert_depth-1 that had their expected_policy_set updated by a PREVIOUS cert's PolicyMappings (which changed it from {IDP} to {SDP}) still carry the SDP in their expected_policy_set. These parent nodes' expected_policy_set is now stale: the mapping that put SDP there has been inhibited, but the parent was not reverted.

Practical impact: At the next cert (depth+1), when matching against this parent's expected_policy_set, the SDP would be matched instead of the IDP. This creates a situation where inhibiting mapping at cert N still allows the mapped policy (SDP) to be matched at cert N+1.

The PKITS §4.11 tests cover this scenario and should catch it. If §4.11.1/4.11.3/4.11.5/4.11.6 pass, then either (a) the PKITS certs are structured such that this path is never triggered, or (b) the issue is masked. Recommend adding a test specifically for the stale expected_policy_set case.

Location: pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1863-1878 (policy_mapping==0 branch)

Fix: When deleting a node with valid_policy=IDP at cert_depth, walk parent nodes at cert_depth-1 and revert their expected_policy_set: replace any SDP (that was put there by the now-inhibited mapping) with the original IDP. Alternatively, store the pre-mapping expected_policy_set and restore it on inhibition.
title: PolicyMappings: inhibited case may leave stale expected_policy_set
